obtained.how: Dalhousie University's institutional repository (DalSpace, now dal.scholaris.ca), item hdl:10222/13475, bitstream v19_p4_a3_Smith_fish_population_Lake_Jesse_Nova_Scotia.pdf; a scanned PDF with no text layer (39 pages), read on the page images

bibliography.checked_against: the first and last pages of the article (page images) and the repository record
bibliography.note: M. W. Smith, Atlantic Biological Station, St. Andrews, N.B.; 'The fish population of Lake Jesse, Nova Scotia'; Proc. Nova Scotian Inst. Sci. Vol. XIX, Pt. 4, pp. 389-427 (received May 9, 1938). The issue (part) number 4 could be added. The repository's author authority ('Smith, Michael W., 1944-') is wrong, but the article itself is clear.

claims.claim: Lake Jesse, Nova Scotia, an 18-ha soft-water lake of 2.4 m mean depth
claims.quote: forty-five acres, a maximum depth of 6.6 metres, and an average depth of 2.4 metres
claims.conditions: depths as of 30 May 1929; the same page says 'The waters are soft' (pH 6.5 at the surface, 6.3 at 6.5 m, 1 August 1934); unstratified in summer

claims.claim: Lake Jesse held no young white perch at all in 1934
claims.quote: White perch fry, however, appeared to be completely absent.
claims.conditions: whole-lake copper sulphate kill on 3 August 1934, fish counted along one-eleventh of the shoreline; killifish and yellow perch fry were found, though scarce
claims.note: Smith offers two explanations: a complete failure of the 1934 spawning, or no spawning at all, the white perch being immigrants (the same was apparently true of neighbouring Tedford Lake). The paper's use as a year-class 'failure' should mention the second possibility.

claims.claim: Lake Jesse, a shallow soft-water lake in Nova Scotia without bass or pickerel
claims.location: abstract, p. 389 (PDF p. 1); Table 1, p. 394 (PDF p. 6)
claims.quote: Predator species, Perca and Morone, constituted 57 per cent of the population.
claims.conditions: species present: brook trout, golden shiner, creek chub, white sucker, brown bullhead, American eel, banded killifish, yellow perch, white perch, ninespine stickleback
claims.note: no bass or pickerel in the species list or Table 1

claims.location: Table 1, p. 394 (PDF p. 6); abstract p. 389 (PDF p. 1)
claims.quote: The estimated population was 36,035 fish, or a production of 19.9 pounds per acre.
claims.conditions: standing crop estimated from fish killed by copper sulphate (3 August 1934) and counted on shore sections making up one-eleventh of the shoreline, weighed after 5-6 months in formalin (perciform fish gain weight in formalin, killifish and eels lose it); some eels survived, so eels are under-counted
claims.note: 19.9 lb/acre × 0.4536 kg/lb ÷ 0.4047 ha/acre = 22.3 kg/ha. Table 1 totals 35,025 fish (the abstract says 36,035), 405,066 g = 893.0 lb, 776 fish and 19.9 lb per acre; yellow perch were 40.5 % of numbers, bullhead 5.1 and white perch 5.5 lb/acre.

notes: The repository's TEXT bundle is empty (39 bytes), so the article was read on the page images rendered by findin --image (pages 1-8, 30, 39). Other useful points: the population was dominated by fish in their second to fourth years; white perch in the 2nd, 3rd and 4th years were 32.7, 35.4 and 21.4 % of the white perch; the abstract notes a scarcity of fry in certain years suggesting cycles of dominant year classes. A companion 'survey of Lake Jesse' (Smith 1938, Proc. N.S. Inst. Sci. 19: 253-263) has the hydrology.
